en.title: Beijing relaxes property purchase restrictions

pattern.title: Labor Supply as the Binding Constraint
pattern.before: Prior to the 2020s, US labor markets operated with relative slack from globalization and demographic trends, keeping wage growth moderate.
pattern.shift: Since the early 2020s, immigration restrictions and demographic shifts tightened labor supply, making wage pressure a persistent feature of economic cycles.
pattern.now: The July 2026 jobs report confirms that this tightness remains, with employers competing for workers and wages rising steadily, even as economic growth faces other headwinds.
pattern.conclusion: The US economy is structurally constrained by labor supply rather than demand; any policy or growth impulse now quickly translates into wage and inflation pressures, limiting the Fed's room to ease.

insight.title: Labor supply constraint redefines US macroeconomic trade-offs
insight.formula: Tightening labor supply + Fiscal expansion → Persistent wage pressure → Elevated inflation → Higher-for-longer rates → Strong dollar
insight.explanation: With immigration-strained labor supply, any boost to demand now immediately pressures wages and inflation, forcing the Fed to maintain restrictive rates. This dynamic keeps the dollar strong, creating a feedback loop that further constrains domestic growth.
